## Root cause
`logparse.py`, line 5:
```python
_KV_RE = re.compile(r'(\w+)="(.*)"')
```
The value-capturing group `(.*)` is greedy and `.` matches any character (including `"`). On a line with multiple `key="value"` pairs, this causes the regex to match from the first `"` all the way to the *last* `"` in the line, swallowing every subsequent pair into the first match's value — exactly the symptom in the bug report (`{'user': 'alice" action="login" result="ok'}`).

## Fix
Changed the value group from `.*` to `[^"]*`, so it can only match characters up to (not including) the next quote, causing each match to stop at its own closing quote:
```python
_KV_RE = re.compile(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"')
```
This still allows spaces inside a value (e.g. `msg="disk almost full"`) since spaces aren't excluded — only the quote character is — satisfying the "keep spaces" requirement from the bug report notes.

## Verification
- Before the fix, `run_tests` showed 3 failing tests: `test_parse_multiple_pairs`, `test_parse_pair_among_other_text`, `test_value_with_spaces_is_kept_whole`, each showing the "everything glommed into one value" symptom described in the bug report, while `test_parse_single_pair`, `test_get_level`, `test_is_error` passed.
- After applying the one-line regex fix, the full suite re-ran automatically: all 6 tests pass, including the previously failing ones, with no regressions in `get_level`/`is_error` behavior (as expected, since `_LEVEL_RE` was untouched).

tool_input.new_content:
"""Parse structured fields out of application log lines."""

import re

_KV_RE = re.compile(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"')
_LEVEL_RE = re.compile(r"\b(DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR)\b")


def parse_kv(line):
    """Return a dict of the ``key="value"`` pairs found in ``line``."""
    return dict(_KV_RE.findall(line))


def get_level(line):
    """Return the log level token in ``line``, or ``None``."""
    match = _LEVEL_RE.search(line)
    return match.group(1) if match else None


def is_error(line):
    """True if the line is at ERROR level."""
    return get_level(line) == "ERROR"
